title: The US Just Charged Lawrence Bishnoi With Ordering the Nijjar Murder. The Indictment Pointedly Clears India's Government.
excerpt: 'Operation Hard Ball' charged 37 defendants tied to three India-based crime syndicates. Prosecutors say they preyed on diaspora communities through murder and extortion.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Lawrence Bishnoi charged with orchestrating Nijjar's assassination, highlighting organized crime's reach.
  • Operation Hard Ball targets 37 defendants across three crime syndicates linked to Indian diaspora.
  • Authorities seized 1,000 kg of cocaine, 12 firearms, and $40,000 in cash during the operation.
  • Bishnoi maintained control of his empire from prison using smuggled phones to direct activities.
  • Indictments reveal a climate of fear among Indian diaspora communities exploited by organized crime.

Lawrence Bishnoi ran a global criminal empire from an Indian jail cell with a smuggled phone. On Tuesday, the United States government told the world exactly what he did with it. A federal indictment unsealed in Los Angeles charges Bishnoi, 33, and his North American deputy Satinderjeet Singh — known as "Goldy Brar" — with directing the June 2023 assassination of Hardeep Singh Nijjar, the Sikh separatist leader who was gunned down by two masked men outside the Guru Nanak Sikh Gurdwara in Surrey, British Columbia. It was a killing that detonated a diplomatic crisis between Canada and India, expelled ambassadors, and strained one of the world's most consequential bilateral relationships. But perhaps the most significant element of the indictment is what it doesn't say. Not once do prosecutors allege that the Indian government was involved in or aware of the assassination. ## Operation Hard Ball The Bishnoi charges are part of a far larger sweep. Under "Operation Hard Ball," U.S. and Canadian authorities have charged 37 defendants across three separate indictments targeting India-based organized crime groups. Twenty-four suspects have been arrested across the United States, Canada and Europe. The investigation is staggering in scope: authorities seized approximately 1,000 kilograms of cocaine, one kilogram of heroin, 12 firearms and $40,000 in cash. From March 2024 to July 2025 alone, the Bishnoi enterprise allegedly stole 520 kilograms of cocaine from rival drug trafficking organizations in the Los Angeles area. First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bilal Essayli didn't mince words. "These criminal organisations have engaged in widespread violence, including targeted killings, extortions, and kidnappings," he said at a press conference in Los Angeles. The organizations "preyed in particular on communities in the United States and Canada with ties to India and routinely extorted these individuals and their family members in India by threatening them with physical harm and death." ## How Bishnoi Ran It From Behind Bars According to the indictment, Bishnoi has been incarcerated since 2015 but maintained operational control of his criminal empire through smuggled cellphones. He allegedly provided co-conspirators with photographs and multiple addresses of Nijjar to facilitate the killing. Singh, described as Bishnoi's childhood friend, directed the gang's North American operations. Brar remains at large, while Bishnoi sits in an Indian prison. Seven of the ten remaining fugitives are believed to be in the United States, two in India, and one in Europe. The indictment describes a deliberate strategy of creating a "climate of fear" among Indian diaspora communities worldwide. The gang publicized its violent acts through online videos, social media posts and media interviews to amplify its reputation — then exploited that fear to extort victims. In one instance, prosecutors allege the gang demanded a $5 million extortion payment from a victim in California. Canada designated the Bishnoi enterprise a terrorist entity in September 2025. ## The Two Other Syndicates Operation Hard Ball didn't stop at Bishnoi. Two other India-based crime groups face indictments. The Bhagwanpuria gang, run by imprisoned gangster Jaggu Bhagwanpuria, is described as a roughly 1,000-member transnational syndicate that specialized in murder-for-hire, weapons trafficking, and elaborate extortion schemes. Prosecutors allege the group colluded with corrupt Indian law enforcement officers to fabricate criminal charges against rivals and extended its extortion operations to families in California and Ohio.
Bishnoi's Criminal Network
›Bishnoi directed operations from prison since 2015.
›Gang extorted victims, demanding up to $5 million.
›Seven fugitives linked to Bishnoi believed to be in the U.S.
›Gang publicized violence to instill fear in diaspora communities.
The third indictment targets another network involved in racketeering and drug trafficking, with operations spanning the Sacramento and Los Angeles areas. Agents executed 23 search warrants in Sacramento and 11 in Los Angeles. ## What the Indictment Means for India-Canada Relations The Nijjar killing was the single most destabilizing event in India-Canada relations in decades. When then-Prime Minister Justin Trudeau publicly stated in September 2023 that Canadian authorities were "actively pursuing credible allegations" linking Indian government agents to the murder, New Delhi called the claim absurd. Both countries expelled diplomats. Trade talks froze. The U.S. indictment offers India a significant diplomatic gift. By attributing the murder to the Bishnoi organized crime group — a private criminal enterprise, not a state operation — it provides a counter-narrative to the allegation of Indian government complicity. Canadian police had arrested four Indian nationals in 2024 in connection with the shooting and said they were investigating potential government ties. The U.S. indictment does not name those alleged shooters as defendants, referring to them only as co-conspirators. Relations between Ottawa and New Delhi have already begun thawing under Prime Minister Mark Carney, who visited India in February on his first official trip and opened negotiations on a trade deal expected to close by November. But some Sikh community groups have criticized Carney for failing to hold India accountable or protect Sikh Canadians from what they describe as transnational repression. ## The Diaspora Warning For the 4.8 million people of Indian origin in the United States and millions more in Canada, the indictments paint an unsettling picture. These were not distant gangs operating in abstract spaces. They were criminal enterprises that specifically targeted Indian diaspora communities — extorting families across continents, threatening relatives in India, running cocaine through the same cities where Indian professionals live and work.
Impact on India-Canada Relations
›Nijjar's murder strained India-Canada relations significantly.
›U.S. indictment clears Indian government of involvement.
›Diplomatic tensions led to expulsion of ambassadors.
›Trade negotiations between India and Canada are resuming.
The message from U.S. prosecutors is clear: these networks are being dismantled. But the scale of the operations — three syndicates, 37 defendants, three continents — suggests that the intersection of Indian organized crime and North American diaspora communities is deeper and more entrenched than most people realized. *Sources: Reuters, CNN, IANS, Fox LA, Bhaskar English, Devdiscourse*
